cases.exposure_context_quote: A 21-year-old male presented to our emergency department on 8 August 2022, after intentionally ingesting 200 mL of diquat the previous day.
cases.agent_quote: after intentionally ingesting 200 mL of diquat the previous day
cases.circumstance: Intentional (suicidal) ingestion of 200 mL of diquat the day before presentation; two sessions of unspecified blood perfusion at another hospital with poor effect.

symptoms.quote: He was diagnosed with pesticide poisoning (diquat poisoning), pulmonary infection, multi-organ dysfunction (heart, lung, kidney), fatty liver, metabolic acidosis, hypoproteinemia, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

He was diagnosed with pesticide poisoning (diquat poisoning), pulmonary infection, multi-organ dysfunction (heart, lung, kidney), fatty liver, metabolic acidosis, hypoproteinemia, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

The chest computed tomography (CT) showed scattered ground-glass opacities and cord-like shadows in the lower lobes of both lungs, decreased liver density suggestive of fatty liver, gastrointestinal fluid and gas accumulation with scattered air-fluid levels, and dilated colon.

cases.time_to_care: presented the day after ingestion; had two sessions of blood perfusion at another hospital before transfer

labs.name: diquat plasma concentration
labs.quote: Laboratory tests revealed a diquat plasma concentration of 3125.47 ng/ml

treatment.name: blood perfusion (at another hospital)
treatment.quote: He had undergone two sessions of blood perfusion (unspecified) at another hospital with poor therapeutic effect.

treatment.name: CRRT and HP
treatment.quote: CRRT and HP were performed, combined with antioxidant therapy, anti-infection, enema, and catharsis.

cases.icu_admission: yes (transferred to ICU and nephrology department)
cases.outcome: survived, discharged 12 September with obvious improvement; at 3-month follow-up diquat undetectable and blood routine, liver, kidney, coagulation function normal
cases.outcome_quote: he was discharged on 12 September after obvious improvement. During the follow-up of 3 months, the blood concentration of diquat was undetectable, and there were no abnormalities in the blood routine, liver function, kidney function, or coagulation function.
cases.notes: Diagnoses also included fatty liver, metabolic acidosis, hypoproteinemia.

cases.exposure_context_quote: A 19-year-old female presented to our emergency department on 24 March 2023, with a history of intentional ingestion of 120 ml of diquat 10 h before.
cases.agent_quote: intentional ingestion of 120 ml of diquat 10 h before
cases.circumstance: Intentional ingestion of 120 mL of diquat 10 h before presentation.

symptoms.finding: inflammatory nodules left lower lung lobe on chest CT
symptoms.quote: The chest CT revealed inflammatory nodules in the left lower lobe of the lung.

labs.name: diquat plasma concentration
labs.quote: Laboratory tests showed a diquat plasma concentration of 5591.6 ng/ml

treatment.name: symptomatic treatment (cefmetazole, lactulose, fluid replacement)
treatment.quote: She was diagnosed with diquat poisoning and treated with symptomatic treatment, including cefmetazole, lactulose, and fluid replacement.

treatment.name: catharsis, anti-infection, antioxidant, blood perfusion and CRRT, hepatoprotective and gastric protective therapy
treatment.quote: She was then transferred to the ICU for further therapy, including catharsis, anti-infection therapy, antioxidant treatment, blood purification (blood perfusion and CRRT), and hepatoprotective and gastric protective approaches based on multidisciplinary consultations.

cases.outcome: survived; requested voluntary discharge on March 29; good survival condition at 3-month follow-up with normal labs and undetectable diquat
cases.outcome_quote: On March 29th, the patient requested to be discharged voluntarily, and her survival condition was good during follow-up. Follow-up for 3 months showed normal blood routine, liver function, kidney function, or coagulation function, and the concentration of diquat was undetectable.

cases.agent_quote: ingesting 30–40 ml of diquat 2 days prior
cases.circumstance: Ingested 30–40 mL of diquat 2 days prior and vomited a small amount afterward; circumstances (intent) not stated in the text.

symptoms.quote: Physical examination revealed pale skin and sclera, oral mucosal erosion, and non-pitting edema in both lower limbs.

symptoms.finding: brainstem infarction, irregular respiratory rhythm, decreased SpO2, coma
symptoms.quote: On December 2, her condition worsened and she was transferred to the ICU. Brain CT indicated brainstem infarction. Her respiratory rhythm became irregular and the SpO2 was decreased.

labs.name: diquat plasma concentration
labs.quote: Laboratory tests on admission showed a diquat plasma concentration of 2475.1 ng/ml

treatment.name: diuretics, catharsis, fluid replacement, anti-infection therapy, CRRT combined with blood perfusion, hepatoprotective measures
treatment.quote: Treatments including diuretics, catharsis, fluid replacement, anti-infection therapy, CRRT combined with blood perfusion, and hepatoprotective measures were performed.

treatment.name: reducing intracranial pressure, blood perfusion, antioxidant therapy, hepatoprotection, electrolyte regulation, endotracheal intubation, CRRT combined with blood perfusion
treatment.quote: Treatments, including reducing intracranial pressure, blood perfusion, antioxidant therapy, hepatoprotection, electrolyte regulation, endotracheal intubation, and CRRT combined with blood perfusion were given to her

cases.icu_admission: yes (transferred to the ICU on December 2)
cases.outcome: died on December 9 (remained in coma; discharged due to financial difficulties and died the same day)
cases.outcome_quote: Despite these efforts, she remained in a coma and was discharged on December 9 due to financial difficulties. The patient died on December 9th.
cases.sequelae: died; diagnosed with multi-organ damage, rhabdomyolysis, acute renal failure, liver dysfunction, moderate anemia, hyperkalemia, brainstem infarction
cases.notes: Intent of ingestion not stated; heart rate/respiratory rate/BP/SpO2 given (89 bpm, 19 breaths/min, 131/85 mmHg, 92%).

cases.exposure_context_quote: A 14-year-old female with a history of depression for 1 year presented to our emergency department on 5 February 2022, approximately 14 h after intentional ingestion of diquat.
cases.agent_quote: approximately 14 h after intentional ingestion of diquat
cases.circumstance: Intentional ingestion; patient had a 1-year history of depression; underwent gastric lavage at another hospital.

symptoms.finding: mild dyspnea and burning sensation in throat and upper abdomen
symptoms.quote: She experienced mild dyspnea and a burning sensation in her throat and upper abdomen.

symptoms.finding: low urine output and generalized edema
symptoms.quote: The patient had a low urine output and generalized edema.

labs.name: diquat plasma concentration
labs.quote: Laboratory tests showed a diquat plasma concentration of 4512.26 ng/ml

labs.name: eGFR (after treatment)
labs.quote: estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 12.63 ml/min/1.73 m2

labs.name: serum creatinine (3-month follow-up)
labs.quote: Serum creatinine was 287 μmol/L with an eGFR of 20.63 mL/min/1.73 m2, and NT-proBNP was 900 ng/L, indicating chronic renal insufficiency and chronic cardiac dysfunction.

treatment.name: gastric lavage (at another hospital)
treatment.quote: The patient immediately underwent gastric lavage at another hospital.

treatment.name: antioxidant therapy, anti-infection measures, fluid replacement, blood perfusion combined with CRRT
treatment.quote: Treatment approaches, including antioxidant therapy, anti-infection measures, fluid replacement, and blood perfusion combined with CRRT were given.

treatment.name: anti-infection, diuresis, and blood purification
treatment.quote: After symptomatic supportive treatments such as anti-infection, diuresis, and blood purification, the creatinine level decreased significantly, and the patient’s condition stabilized.

cases.icu_admission: UNVERIFIED (no explicit ICU admission stated; managed with blood purification and later nephrology department care)
cases.outcome: survived; condition stabilized and discharged on March 9; at 3-month follow-up diquat undetectable, blood count/liver/coagulation normal, but chronic renal insufficiency and chronic cardiac dysfunction
cases.outcome_quote: The patient was discharged on March 9th. At the 3-month follow-up after discharge, diquat was undetectable in the blood. Complete blood count, liver function, and coagulation parameters were within normal limits. Serum creatinine was 287 μmol/L with an eGFR of 20.63 mL/min/1.73 m2, and NT-proBNP was 900 ng/L, indicating chronic renal insufficiency and chronic cardiac dysfunction.
cases.sequelae: chronic renal insufficiency and chronic cardiac dysfunction at 3-month follow-up
cases.notes: Diagnoses included stage 3 acute kidney injury, liver insufficiency, cardiac insufficiency, depression, gastrointestinal bleeding, pulmonary infection.
